# StudentContext v3

`StudentContextBuilder` constructs a bounded request snapshot for deterministic
teacher policy and later model orchestration. Student facts remain owned by
`ms-go-student` for learner/mastery facts and by Practice for active practice
facts; the context exists only in memory and is never persisted.

## General input

For `general_teacher`, the builder reads Student's exact
`student-learner-overview-v2` projection. It contains optional declared
onboarding, at most 20 recent current mastery rows, the current path, latest
diagnostic, and five recent learning-session summaries. Declared
experience is prompt context only and never substitutes for diagnostics or
mastery evidence. Raw evidence, reducer audit, answers, and unbounded history
are excluded.

## Course task input

Version 1 accepts only an authenticated `student_id` plus a
`learning_action_id`. Teacher does not accept learning targets from a browser
and does not reread mutable Course or practice-catalog targets.

The builder first calls Student's ownership-scoped action context endpoint. The
safe response supplies:

- action, student, task, and contextual identity;
- the immutable ordered target snapshot;
- `OPEN|CLOSED` lifecycle status and `opened_at`.

Objective outcome, answer identity, evidence class, raw evidence, and reducer
audit remain private to Student.

For the same open action, Student may additionally return
`student-learning-action-code-context-v1`. Student alone joins the private
answer to its exact Sandbox. Teacher receives only availability, up to 12
sorted UTF-8 text files, 16 KiB per file and 64 KiB total, plus truncation
metadata. Secret files/lines, dependencies, build artifacts, binaries, and
answer/Sandbox IDs are excluded. It also carries the latest
mutation-invalidated validation/test pass flag, bounded issue count, and time;
raw validator output remains excluded. The snapshot is untrusted prompt data
and is never persisted by Teacher.

Only an `OPEN` `lesson_task` action can use this Student action projection.
For one to 100 frozen targets, the builder asks Student for the current mastery
projection and requires exactly one item per target in the same order. A
targetless action produces empty relevant mastery without inference or a
mastery call.

## Practice/project input

For `practice_task|project`, Teacher reads
`practice-task-teacher-context.v1` directly from the exact Practice Runtime
instance. `PRACTICE_SERVICE_BASE_URL` targets `ms-go-practice-runtime` (the
local default is `http://localhost:8080`; Compose uses
`http://ms-go-practice-runtime:8080`). The configured Teacher token is scoped
to the context, validation-explanation, and assistance routes below, and
Practice Runtime rejects it on every other route. It cannot submit work, retry
validation, review, complete an instance, or deliver Student evidence. The
three route paths and payloads remain the existing §3.2 contract.
It validates instance, student, revision, current public Step/acceptance, exact
versioned targets, effective assistance policy, bounded sanitized workspace,
and validation summary. It then asks Student for mastery only for those targets.
Private checks, reference/negative fixtures, raw validator output, hidden rubric,
and Sandbox identity are forbidden. No legacy Student-runtime fallback exists.

For `practice_task` only, the builder also attempts Practice's separate
`practice-task-teacher-validation-context.v1` read. It accepts an available
explanation only when the exact student, task instance, frozen revision, and
learning action match both the normalized base context and Dialog request.
The prompt receives only submission ID, workspace digest, update time, pass
correlation, and the bounded `teacher-validation-explanation.v1` allowlist (at
most five issues and 16 KiB). Unknown fields, invalid/null combinations,
identity drift, private-looking absolute paths, invalid digests/timestamps, and
Practice's explicit projection-corruption response fail closed. Explicit
unavailable and ordinary dependency failures omit this optional context; they
do not synthesize validation or change the authoritative task state. Project
dialogs never request this projection.

Teacher records Practice/project assistance before Dialog append with the stored
TeacherDecision ID as `usage_id` and its exact `practice_step_id`, action kind,
and nullable hint level. The request carries no caller timestamp or policy.
The production client accepts only a receipt matching usage, instance, student,
step, kind, and nullable hint level, with server policy
`practice-task-assistance-policy.v1` and a nonzero UTC `created_at`. Runtime
replays the first receipt and timestamp for the same stable request even after
lifecycle changes; new assistance retains Runtime's current admission guards.
A pending-body recovery uses the original decision and Dialog source event append
key without generating another answer or loading fresh student context.

## Durable official feedback and live observations

Runtime derives the current validation summary and Teacher explanation from the
latest official validation run's bounded safe summary committed with the official
transition. Reconstructing its PostgreSQL repository, or reading through a new
Runtime process, preserves the same submission, workspace digest, outcome, safe
issues, and deterministic `source_digest`; Teacher does not retain a feedback
cache. Pending validation or retry makes the previous explanation unavailable.
Legacy runs without a stored safe summary remain explicitly unavailable.

An official `FAIL` explains required semantic stage failures through at most five
unique learner-safe blocking issues. An official `ERROR` carries a known technical
classification and safe message, rather than describing a learner mistake. An
official `PASS` has no blocking issues, including failures of optional stages.
Runtime's base-context stage and issue counts come from that same persisted
current summary. Runtime verifies the current submission belongs to the exact instance and owner
and matches the frozen revision and snapshot workspace digest. The strict Teacher
client verifies the student, instance, frozen revision, and action and requires
valid submission metadata before accepting the bounded explanation; repeated
reads of unchanged state preserve its digest.

Local validation/test observations describe current editable workspace behavior
and may be invalidated by mutations. They do not replace the frozen submission's
official result. Teacher explanations are advisory context for guidance: Runtime
alone owns official validation and completion, while Student owns evidence and
mastery. Teacher never reads live files to reconstruct an official explanation,
imports raw validator output, or promotes its advice into an official decision.

The opt-in `integration` test `TestT12RuntimeFeedback` calls the real production
HTTP client against a serialized PostgreSQL-backed Runtime fixture. The driver
provides `T12_RUNTIME_URL`, `T12_TEACHER_TOKEN`, `T12_RUNTIME_READY_FILE`,
`T12_TEACHER_RESULT_FILE`, and `T12_EXPECT_OUTCOME` (`FAIL`, `ERROR`, or `PASS`).
The ready JSON supplies `student_id`, `task_instance_id`, `task_revision_id`,
`learning_action_id`, `submission_id`, `workspace_digest`, `outcome`, and nullable
`error_classification`; an optional `url` must match the selected Runtime URL.
The test obtains its base context from Runtime's actual Teacher endpoint, checks
repeat-read stability and foreign student/action/token rejection, and writes only
the allowlisted public explanation to the result file. It neither launches
services nor invokes an LLM. An unselected ordinary integration suite skips it;
selecting the ready file requires all other inputs. The durable producer's own
PostgreSQL/reconstruction proof remains necessary alongside this consumer proof.

## Failure policy

The outbound adapter uses the exact dedicated Practice Teacher token, a three-second default HTTP
timeout, a 2 MiB base-context response bound, a 32 KiB validation-explanation
response bound, and strict JSON decoding. It fails closed on
transport/auth/server failure, malformed responses, closed actions, identity
mismatch, code-context bound mismatch, or mastery count/order/target mismatch. Version 3 has no cached or
anonymous-personalization fallback.

## Runtime composition

The TeacherOrchestrator constructs this context for mounted `lesson_task`,
`practice_task`, and `project` dialog jobs. The snapshot is passed to
deterministic pedagogy and confidential prompt execution, then discarded.
General and lesson dialogs retain the bounded Student learner overview. V1
lesson overview/selection anchors use the existing current Course revision.
`lesson-message-context.v2` instead requires an exact Student-owned frozen
assignment anchor. Teacher reads
`GET /internal/students/{studentID}/learning-paths/{pathID}/items/{itemID}/lesson-context`
with the existing shared internal read token. The production client requires
one strict `student-assigned-lesson-context.v1` object with exactly
`schema`, `student_id`, `learning_path_id`, `learning_path_item_id`, `course_id`,
`lesson_id`, `lesson_revision_id`, `content_digest`, and
`content: {title, excerpt, description}`. All identities are UUIDs. Title is
bounded to 1000 runes, excerpt to 4000 runes, description to 1 MiB of valid UTF-8,
and the response to 2 MiB. Teacher recomputes `sha256:lowercase64` from Go
`encoding/json.Marshal([3]string{title, excerpt, description})` without trimming
or translating the frozen strings.

V2 verifies owner, exact path/item, course, lesson, immutable revision, digest,
and selected substring before generation. Missing, foreign, malformed, or
unavailable Student context fails closed with zero Course fallback or model
calls. A newer Course publication cannot replace or invalidate this projection.
`LessonTeachingContext` carries the same v2 anchor and only the exact bounded
title/excerpt for overview or selected fragment (at most 12000 runes) for
selection. Full description is transient verification input; it is never added
to prompt variables, history, logs, or Teacher persistence. V1/legacy readable
history stays unchanged; cross-schema or partial v2 anchors cannot downgrade.
A durable pending response still replays delivery without rereading context.

## Curriculum planning

Teacher does not contain a curriculum planner. It recognizes an explicit desired
outcome or a post-session need to replan and sends a bounded, idempotent planning
intent to `ms-go-learning-planner`. That service owns the target/prerequisite
graph, reads Student mastery, generates or reuses canonical Course content,
requests assignment and reconciliation from Student, which stores and applies
changes to the authoritative Learning Path.

This makes a separate Knowledge Tree service unnecessary for the current
platform: the planning-time graph has one owner in Learning Planner. Teacher's
task-scoped teaching pipeline remains graph-free and uses only the exact target
references frozen by Student for the current LearningAction.

Course tasks supply authored targets through Student's frozen action. Practice
supplies exact targets from its frozen v2 task instance. Neither path infers
targets from prose, tags, or mutable catalog state.

## Accepted Evidence/Mastery replan boundary (Problem #4)

The [Hybrid Replanning decision](https://github.com/bemulima/ms-go-learning-planner/blob/main/docs/hybrid-mastery-replanning.md) separates Teacher's request from Planner's
planning decision and Student's safe-boundary application. For this target flow,
Teacher requests evaluation through Student coordination and explains the owner
trace. It cannot compute a substitute route, directly rewrite Student state, or
promise an immediate mutation from a Mastery change. Existing planning transport
contracts above remain current; no new delegation implementation is introduced.
